title: Cedar Analytics on-prem sizing + Terraform upgrade playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for Cedar Analytics' private deployment (VPC/on‑prem) covering capacity assumptions, Terraform module notes, and an upgrade/rollback plan for runtime and infra components. The doc is intentionally lightweight and conversational — intended to be used in sync calls with Cedar SE and infra teams.

High-level goals (customer asks):
- Support 6k concurrent streaming chat sessions at p95 latency < 300ms token generation for short prompts (~128 tokens).
- Data residency: all inference traffic and KV cache kept inside customer VPC; logs persisted to on-prem object store (MinIO).
- FIPS-ready crypto and integration with customer HSM (AWS CloudHSM connected to air-gapped HSM appliance).
- Upgrade path for runtime (v1.6 -> v1.8) with zero-downtime fallback to v1.6.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Customer will provide 8x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs across 2 racks for production (4 GPUs/rack), with RDMA fabric and a 25Gbps leaf network.
- Average request length distribution: 75% short (< 128 tokens), 20% medium (128-512), 5% long (>512).
- Tokenization and KV cache hit rate target: 18% prefix cache hit; caching will reduce GPU work ~12% after warmup.
- On‑prem object store will expose S3-compatible endpoints; expect 300MB/s aggregate read/write for model artifacts during rollout.
- Control-plane connectivity: the customer allows outbound HTTPS to Redwood control plane on port 443 for telemetry; if blocked, we use offline control-plane mode (extra ops overhead).

Sizing rationale (workload -> node counts):
- Perf baseline: our internal benchmark for model M-late@fp16 quantized shows ~120 tokens/s per A100-80 per stream at sequence length 128 with batched continuous serving.
- Concurrency calc: target 6k concurrent sessions -> assume average active token generation 0.8 tokens/s per session => ~4.8k tokens/s aggregate.
- GPUs required: 4.8k tokens/s / 120 tokens/s per GPU = 40 GPUs; apply 1.6x operational buffer -> 64 GPUs.
- Customer constrained to 8 GPUs: propose multi-tier approach:
  - Prod baseline: 8 GPUs + burst to cloud Dedicated capacity for peak shifting via smart routing (preferred short-term).
  - Long-term: plan for 64 GPU footprint on-prem in two phases (capability expansion timeline below).

Temporary hybrid recommendation:
- Stage 1 (0-3 months): Deploy in-customer PoC on 8 GPUs (single rack) with routing policy: 70% local, 30% hosted fallback. Validate latency/cost.
- Stage 2 (3-9 months): Expand to 24 GPUs (add 2 more nodes), enable KV prefix caching and model sharding; reduce hosted fallback to <10%.
- Stage 3 (9-18 months): Full 64 GPU deployment if justified by traffic growth.

Storage & networking notes:
- Model artifacts: store in MinIO; recommend v4 signatures and multipart uploads for large files.
- KV cache: local NVMe per node (recommended 2TB NVMe per GPU-host node); use LRU with fixed serialized shards.
- Shared FS: avoid central NFS for model serving; prefer local copies + background rsync from MinIO.
- Network: require tuned TCP settings (rx/tx buffer increased), enable hugepages for kernel, and ensure RDMA between GPU nodes for multi-GPU cross-node attention kernels.

Terraform module notes (practical items and TODOs):
- Module versions: use terraform-modules/redwood-private/v2.3.0 as baseline. We need two patches in the customer overlay:
  1) add variable 'hsm_key_alias' -> handles HSM-backed KMS integration; patch in PR referenced above.
  2) expose 'local_nvme_size_gb' to allow operator to override default 512GB -> set to 2048 for this customer.
- State management: customer prefers remote state in HashiCorp Vault-backed Consul; our modules currently default to S3. Action: add state backend wrapper (small helper) and document manual bootstrap steps.
- Blue/Green upgrade support: add optional module flag 'service_deploy_strategy' with choices [rolling, blue_green, canary]. Default rolling; for Cedar recommend canary for runtime upgrades.
- Networking: module has 'subnet_tags' and 'rdma_enabled' booleans; confirm with ops that RDMA NICs are plugged into the subnets we will manage.
- Secrets: ensure provider for HSM (pkcs11) is included in Terraform plan; avoid writing any HSM material into plaintext tfstate by using Vault provider secrets.

Upgrade plan (runtime v1.6 -> v1.8) - outline:
- Pre-upgrade checks (T-30d):
  - Run upgrade dry-run in staging with 2 GPUs and synthetic traffic; exercise all model variants.
  - Run backward-compat test of function/tool calling and streaming; validate streaming timeouts.
  - Snapshot current MinIO bucket (versioning on) and export service metrics for baseline.
- Week of upgrade (T-7 to T-0):
  - Lock config: freeze non-essential deploys; communicate maintenance window.
  - Apply Terraform changes to add versioned runtime groups: create runtime-v1.8 ASG (configured as canary).
  - Deploy 1 canary node (1 GPU) running v1.8 internal image; route 1% of traffic for 24h, collect logs and token-level latency.
  - If canary ok -> expand to 10% for 6h -> 50% for 12h -> 100% in 3 steps with health checks after each step.
- Rollback plan:
  - Canary fail criteria: error rate > 0.5% above baseline OR p95 token latency regressions > 20% OR output-quality regression flagged by eval harness.
  - If fail: revert traffic routing to v1.6 immediately and scale down v1.8 group; keep v1.8 nodes for postmortem.

Operational runbook snippets (commands / checks):
- TF apply dry-run: `terraform plan -var-file=cedar-override.tfvars -out plan.bin` then `terraform show -json plan.bin | jq ...` (verify no hsm material written).
- Health checks: `curl -sS https://local-proxy/healthz` and `curl -sS https://local-proxy/metrics | grep token_gen_latency`
- KV cache sanity: `redis-cli --scan` (if using Redis for checkpoint index) and `ls /nvme/cache/shard-* | wc -l`

Architecture Q&A (pulled from sync with Cedar infra):
- Q: Can we use customer NFS to share models between nodes?
  A: Prefer not. NFS introduces latency and single-point-of-failure for large models. Use MinIO + local NVMe sync. Documented fallback in Terraform overlay if customer insists.
- Q: How do we meet FIPS/HSM requirement?
  A: Integrate PKCS#11 provider via Vault and the Terraform HSM module. Ensure runtime signs keys via HSM (no plaintext keys in tfstate). This requires HSM ops to provision aliases in advance.
- Q: What about backups for patient/PII logs?
  A: Configure object lifecycle retention in MinIO and route sensitive logs to customer secure SIEM; avoid sending any PII to Redwood control plane.

Open items (blocking or to validate):
- Confirm exact GPU model (are A100-80GB guaranteed or mixed A100-40/80?). Impacts token/s estimates.
- Customer network egress policy: confirm port 443 outbound allowance for control-plane telemetry. If blocked, we need manual operator flows and longer SLAs.
- Vault/Consul remote state bootstrap: who owns? Cedar or Redwood infra team?
- HSM appliance model and ops SLA for key rotation (required before TF run).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: actual request length distribution skews longer -> GPUs insufficient. Mitigation: limit user token window via prompt engineering, rate-limit long requests, and maintain hosting fallback.
- Risk: Terraform state leakage of HSM material. Mitigation: use Vault provider and stricter provider config, manual state review in PR with security team.

Next steps / proposed timeline (high level):
- Week 0: Align on open items; confirm GPU model and network policy.
- Week 1-2: Patch Terraform overlay (hsm_key_alias, local_nvme_size_gb), get PR reviewed (see linked PR).
- Week 3-6: PoC deploy on 8 GPUs, basic traffic routing to hosted fallback enabled.
- Month 2-6: Expand to 24 GPUs, enable caching and reduce fallback.

Notes to self / meeting prep bullets for next call with Cedar:
- Bring sample latency numbers from PoC run and compare with internal bench for M-late@fp16.
- Ask for weekend maintenance window for canary expansion.
- Confirm who has admin access to MinIO and HSM.

Appendix (quick checklist for Terraform bootstrap):
- Ensure Vault path `secret/cedar/private-deploy` exists and has `hsm_key_alias` and `minio_creds`
- Customer to create service account with S3 write and read for model artifacts
- Initial TF run: use `-target=module.bootstrap` to provision network and state backend before full apply

-- end draft --

Comments welcome — please add inline notes in the PR or slack @ashamenon for anything that needs clarifying.
